scenario: A client secret for an app registration with Azure roles is saved in a script or CI system, exposed, and used to read and copy firm data
threat_source: External actor using a leaked credential
affected_assets: Every resource the service principal can reach; deal and investor files in storage
treatment: Replace secrets with managed identities or federated credentials, scope deployment identities to resource groups, and alert on role assignment changes

scenario: A storage container or account open to anonymous or all-network access makes diligence material readable from the internet
threat_source: Staff or automation misconfiguration; opportunistic scanning
affected_assets: Diligence exports, board packs, investor reports in blob storage
owner_role: Data owner with cloud platform owner
treatment: Disallow anonymous blob access, set the storage firewall to Deny, disable Shared Key, and watch Defender for Storage alerts

scenario: A Global Administrator elevates into Azure and the User Access Administrator assignment at root is left in place, then the account is phished
affected_assets: Every management group and subscription in the tenant
treatment: Keep the elevate-access toggle off outside recorded tasks, alert on elevation events, and require MFA for Azure management

scenario: Backups are deleted or their retention reduced by a compromised administrator session and no protected copy exists
threat_source: Ransomware operator or privileged user error
affected_assets: Virtual machines, databases, and file data for the firm's workloads
treatment: Protect production VMs with Azure Backup, keep vault soft delete, lock immutability, and prove a restore within the review window

scenario: A Defender for Cloud alert is raised but reaches an unmonitored inbox, so a compromise continues for weeks
threat_source: Any intrusion that Defender for Cloud detects
affected_assets: Whichever workload the alert concerns; investigation evidence
treatment: Name a shared monitored security contact, notify on High severity and Owner role, and test action groups after each change

scenario: The identity provider or Conditional Access misconfiguration locks administrators out of Azure during an incident and no tested emergency path exists
threat_source: Provider outage, misconfiguration, or attack on the provider
affected_assets: Administrative access to every subscription during an incident
treatment: Keep emergency access accounts designed per M365-04, reach Azure only through elevation, and rehearse the path quarterly

scenario: A standing Owner assignment held by someone whose role no longer needs it is used in a mistake or hijacked session that deletes or exposes resources
treatment: Make Owner and User Access Administrator eligible through PIM with MFA, approval, and bounded duration, and review assignments quarterly

scenario: A virtual machine with RDP or SSH open to the internet is brute forced and used as a foothold
threat_source: External actor scanning for exposed management ports
affected_assets: The VM, its managed identity, and the networks it can reach
treatment: Remove internet management rules, reach VMs through Azure Bastion, and alert on NSG changes

scenario: A key vault or its secrets are purged by a compromised administrator and the data they protect becomes unreadable
threat_source: Attacker covering tracks or administrator error
affected_assets: Secrets, keys, and anything encrypted with them, including backups
treatment: Enable purge protection, use the RBAC permission model scoped to the vault, and log AuditEvent to the central workspace

scenario: Activity Log and resource logs are not retained or exported, so the firm cannot reconstruct who changed what after an incident
threat_source: Attacker covering tracks or missing configuration
affected_assets: Audit trail for every subscription; incident investigation
treatment: Export the Activity Log to a central workspace, keep it beyond 90 days, route resource logs, and alert on policy assignment deletion

scenario: Compromised credentials are used for cryptomining or bulk resource creation and the firm learns from the invoice
affected_assets: Subscription spend and the compromised subscription's resources
owner_role: Finance operations owner with cloud platform owner
treatment: Set budgets with actual and forecast alerts, enable anomaly alerts, restrict allowed locations, and treat alerts as security triage items

scenario: A subscription is transferred out of the firm's directory or a foreign subscription is moved in, escaping the firm's policies and billing oversight
threat_source: Insider or external actor with billing permissions
affected_assets: Subscriptions, their data, and the firm's governed hierarchy
treatment: Keep both subscription transfer policies at Allow no users, route new subscriptions to a governed default management group, and require authorization to create management groups
